timeline_list.title: The inspiration
timeline_list.description: Shichinin no Samurai (Seven Samurai, 1954), by Akira Kurosawa (1910-1998), serves as the inspiration for the Hollywood production The Magnificent Seven (1960).

timeline_list.title: Psycho
timeline_list.description: Psycho (1960), by Alfred Hitchcock (1899-1980), changes cinema forever with its approach to violence and sexuality and a never-bettered use of the MacGuffin.

timeline_list.title: The "Evil Children" Subgenre
timeline_list.description: One of the first films in the "evil children" subgenre, Village of the Damned (1960) is a faithful adaptation of John Wyndham's novel The Midwich Cuckoos.

timeline_list.title: The French New Wave and the British New Wave
timeline_list.description: The French New Wave breathes new life into cinema with À bout de souffle (Breathless, 1960), as does the British New Wave with Saturday Night and Sunday Morning (1960).

timeline_list.title: Disregarding Conventional Narrative
timeline_list.description: The Italian epic La dolce vita (1960) disregards conventional narrative.

timeline_list.title: Fright Break
timeline_list.description: Influenced by Psycho (1960), William Castle (1914-1977) releases Homicidal (1961). This first film of the Jason genre includes a "fright break" for those too scared to watch.

timeline_list.title: West Side Story
timeline_list.description: West Side Story (1961) is released. The following year it wins 10 Oscars, more than any other musical.

timeline_list.title: Spaghetti Western
timeline_list.description: Tierra brutal (The Savage Guns, 1961) marks the arrival of a new genre – the spaghetti Western. The film is shot in Almería, a very popular Spanish location.

timeline_list.title: Civil Rights
timeline_list.description: In the US, the civil rights movement against racism gains momentum, and lawyer Atticus Finch comes to the screen in To Kill a Mockingbird (1962).

timeline_list.title: Glauber's Debut
timeline_list.description: In Brazil, director Glauber Rocha (1939-1981), herald of Cinema Novo, makes his debut with Barravento (The Turning Wind, 1962).

timeline_list.title: The Importance of Spy Films
timeline_list.description: United Artists releases two of the most important spy films: The Manchurian Candidate (1962) and Dr. No (1962) (the first James Bond film).

timeline_list.title: Marilyn Monroe
timeline_list.description: Marilyn Monroe (1926-1962) dies. The Misfits (1961), released the year before, was her last appearance on the big screen.

timeline_list.title: A Palme d'Or for Brazil
timeline_list.description: O Pagador de Promessas (The Given Word, 1962) wins the Palme d'Or at the Cannes Film Festival, something unprecedented for Brazil until then.

timeline_list.title: Haunted House
timeline_list.description: The Haunting (1963), Martin Scorsese's (b. 1942) favorite horror film, is the definitive haunted house story. It influenced Shutter Island (2010).

timeline_list.title: Giallo
timeline_list.description: Mario Bava (1914-1980) releases what is considered the first giallo film (an Italian literary and film genre in which killers are typically pursued by detectives), La ragazza che sapeva troppo (The Girl Who Knew Too Much, 1963) – a salute to Hitchcock.

timeline_list.title: A New Milestone
timeline_list.description: In 1963, Sidney Poitier (b. 1927) made history by becoming the first Black actor ever to win the Academy Award for Best Actor, for his performance in the drama Lilies of the Field (1963).

timeline_list.title: Beating the Censors
timeline_list.description: After a hard-fought battle with the censors, The Pawnbroker (1965), directed by Sidney Lumet (b. 1924), is released. The film features bare breasts.

timeline_list.title: Sergio Leone Enters the Scene
timeline_list.description: Per un pugno di dollari (A Fistful of Dollars, 1964), by Sergio Leone (1929-1989), is released – to this day the high point of the Spaghetti Western.

timeline_list.title: I Am Cuba
timeline_list.description: Soviet director Mikhail Kalatozov (1903-1973) makes Soy Cuba (I Am Cuba, 1964).

timeline_list.title: Spaghetti Western and Comedy
timeline_list.description: Cavalca e uccidi (Ride and Kill, 1964) is one of the first spaghetti Western comedies.

timeline_list.title: The Last Gasps of the French New Wave
timeline_list.description: The French New Wave enjoys one last moment of splendor with Alphaville (1965) and Pierrot le fou (Pierrot le Fou, 1965), by Jean-Luc Godard (b. 1930).

timeline_list.title: Reinvigorating the Musical
timeline_list.description: The Sound of Music (1965) beats Gone with the Wind (1939) at the box office, reinvigorating the musical genre.

timeline_list.title: The Last Black-and-White Oscar
timeline_list.description: Who's Afraid of Virginia Woolf? (1966) is the last film to win an Academy Award in the Black-and-White category.

timeline_list.title: Clint Eastwood
timeline_list.description: Il buono, il brutto, il cattivo (The Good, the Bad and the Ugly, 1966) cements Clint Eastwood (b. 1930) as an icon, "The Man with No Name".

timeline_list.title: Films for the Young
timeline_list.description: The Graduate (1967) and Bonnie and Clyde (1967) represent a new kind of youth-oriented studio film.

timeline_list.title: Planet of the Apes
timeline_list.description: Planet of the Apes (1968) – at once a Swiftian satire and a Flash Gordon adventure – sets the precedent for future science fiction franchises.

timeline_list.title: Zombies
timeline_list.description: Night of the Living Dead (1968) is released, kicking off "zombie movies" and making George A. Romero (b. 1940) the father of the subgenre.

timeline_list.title: Definitive Science Fiction
timeline_list.description: 2001: A Space Odyssey (1968) premieres. A collaboration between Stanley Kubrick (1928-1999) and writer Arthur C. Clarke, it is conceived as the definitive science fiction film.

timeline_list.title: Once Upon a Time in the West
timeline_list.description: C'era una volta il West (Once Upon a Time in the West, 1968) legitimizes the genre among critics and has since been considered by many to be Sergio Leone's (1929-1989) best film.

timeline_list.title: Fespaco Festival
timeline_list.description: The first edition of the Fespaco Festival takes place in Ouagadougou, Burkina Faso. The biennial event is crucial to the future of African cinema.
